Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence "Wikipedia:Verifiability")._(June 2023)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance\_template\_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

Following the _Static Age_ sessions, the Misfits began a shift in songwriting and appearance, with Danzig writing more songs inspired by [B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B_movie "B movie") horror and science fiction films. He painted skeletal patterns on his performance clothing, while Only began applying dark makeup around his eyes and styling his hair in a long point hanging from his forehead between his eyes and down to his chin, a style that became known as a "[devilock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devilock "Devilock")" and which both Danzig and Only's brother Doyle would eventually adopt. This new style and musical direction would later be described as the [subgenre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subgenre "Subgenre") "[horror punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_punk "Horror punk")".

The band performed more frequently and embarked on short tours in support of the _Bullet_ single. While in Canada in October 1978 Coma quit the band because he did not enjoy touring, and guitarist Rick Riley filled in temporarily to finish the tour. Mr. Jim also quit following the tour, citing a distaste for the horror direction in which the band was heading. Within two months the pair were replaced by drummer [Joey Poole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Image "Joey Image"), under the pseudonym Joey Image, and guitarist Robert Kaufhold, also known as [Bobby Steele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Steele "Bobby Steele"). The new lineup of Danzig, Only, Image, and Steele began performing in December 1978 and continued to evolve the horror elements of the band. They released the _[Horror Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror\_Business "Horror Business")_ single in June 1979, the cover of which featured a skeletal figure inspired by a poster for the 1946 [film serial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serial_(film) "Serial (film)")_[The Crimson Ghost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crimson\_Ghost "The Crimson Ghost")_.

The figure became a [mascot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mascot "Mascot") for the band, and its skull image would serve as the Misfits' logo for the rest of their career. The band also launched a [fan club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_club "Fan club") named the "Fiend Club" which Danzig operated in a [do-it-yourself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do_it_yourself "Do it yourself") fashion from his mother's basement in Lodi, [silkscreening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen-printing "Screen-printing")[T-shirts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-shirt "T-shirt"), assembling records, mailing merchandise catalogs, booking shows for the band, and answering [fan mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_mail "Fan mail").

In June 1979, the Misfits performed as openers for [The Damned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Damned_(band) "The Damned (band)") in New York City. Only spoke with singer [Dave Vanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Vanian "Dave Vanian") about the possibility of the Misfits touring the United Kingdom with The Damned. That November the band released the _[Night of the Living Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night\_of\_the\_Living\_Dead\_(song) "Night of the Living Dead (song)")_ single and flew to England to tour with The Damned. Upon arriving there, however, they learned that Vanian had not taken his conversation with Only seriously and had not planned on having the Misfits on the tour. Vanian attempted to arrange for the Misfits to take part in the tour, but the band members were unhappy with the situation and left the tour after only two shows. Image then quit the band and flew back to the United States. With their return flight not scheduled until late December, the remaining band members stayed in London. Only spent time with [Sid Vicious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sid_Vicious "Sid Vicious")' mother, Anne Ritchie, whom he had befriended after Vicious' death in February 1979. Danzig and Steele got into a fight with [skinheads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skinhead "Skinhead") while waiting to see [The Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Jam "The Jam"), were arrested, and spent two nights in jail in [Brixton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brixton "Brixton"). This experience inspired the later song "London Dungeon". Although in an interview on podcast San Clemente Punk, Bobby Steele tells a completely different version of the events.

Upon their return to the United States the Misfits released the _[Beware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beware\_(EP) "Beware (EP)")_[EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") in January 1980, then took a four-month break before adding [Arthur McGuckin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Googy "Arthur Googy") as their new drummer under the pseudonym Arthur Googy. During this time Only's younger brother [Paul Caiafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Caiafa "Paul Caiafa"), a longtime fan of the band who went by the nickname Doyle, began learning to play guitar with help from Danzig and Only. The Misfits began working on an album which they planned to release through their Plan 9 label, recording twelve songs in a studio in August 1980. Doyle practiced with the band and loaned the band his gear for recording. That October Steele was ejected from the band, when Steele no-showed a scheduled recording session, in favor of the sixteen-year-old Doyle. Steele went on to form [The Undead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Undead "The Undead"), while Doyle made his debut with the Misfits at their annual [Halloween](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halloween "Halloween") performance at [Irving Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fillmore_New_York_at_Irving_Plaza "The Fillmore New York at Irving Plaza") in New York City. After several more performances, the band took another hiatus for six months.

After reconvening, the band selected three of the twelve songs from their August 1980 album sessions and released them as _[3 Hits From Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3\_Hits\_From\_Hell "3 Hits From Hell")_ in April 1981. Throughout the rest of 1981 they continued to record tracks for a full-length album, to be titled _[Walk Among Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk\_Among\_Us "Walk Among Us")_. They had planned to release it through Plan 9 but instead accepted an offer from [Slash Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slash_Records "Slash Records"), deciding to rework the album before its release. In October 1981 they released two more tracks from the August 1980 sessions as the _[Halloween](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halloween\_(The\_Misfits\_song) "Halloween (The Misfits song)")_ single. On November 20 they recorded a performance at Broadway in San Francisco.

[Black Flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Flag_(band) "Black Flag (band)") were also performing that night at the [Mabuhay Gardens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mabuhay_Gardens "Mabuhay Gardens") downstairs on Broadway, and Black Flag singer [Henry Rollins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Rollins "Henry Rollins"), a longtime fan of the band, came up to watch the Misfits' [soundcheck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundcheck "Soundcheck"). He stayed to watch the band's set and sang guest vocals on "[We Are 138](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_138 "We Are 138")". The two bands crossed paths again on Christmas in Lodi, where Black Flag wound up playing as the opening band for the [Necros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necros "Necros") and the Misfits.

### 1982–1983: Albums and dissolution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1982–1983: Albums and dissolution")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/Doyle-misfits.jpg/250px-Doyle-misfits.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Doyle-misfits.jpg)

[Doyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doyle_Wolfgang_von_Frankenstein "Doyle Wolfgang von Frankenstein") performing with the Misfits at the Wilson Center in Washington, D.C. in 1982

_Walk Among Us_ was released in March 1982 through [Ruby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Records "Ruby Records") and Slash Records. It was the first full-length Misfits album to be properly released, and the only album to be released while the early incarnation of the band was still active. A national tour in support of the album followed, and the band's performances began to grow more intense and violent. Danzig and Googy clashed frequently during the tour, and after a heated argument at a [McDonald's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's "McDonald's") restaurant Danzig kicked Googy out of the band, delaying their plans to record their next EP. They offered the vacant drummer position to their friend [Eerie Von](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eerie_Von "Eerie Von"), who had served as their occasional [roadie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roadie "Roadie") and photographer, but he had already committed to drumming for [Rosemary's Babies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary's_Babies "Rosemary's Babies"). Henry Rollins recommended former Black Flag drummer [Robo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robo_(musician) "Robo (musician)"), who flew to New Jersey to join the Misfits in July 1982. Doyle graduated from high school and he and Only began working full-time at their father's machine shop, earning money to purchase new instruments, fund the band's tours, and press records, while Danzig ran the Fiend Club and continued writing new songs.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In September 1982 the Misfits embarked on a national tour, with the [Necros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necros "Necros") as their opening act. During the tour they stopped at a studio to record the instrumental tracks for their next EP. They were arrested in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") on charges of [grave robbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grave_robbing "Grave robbing") while attempting to locate the grave of [voodoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Voodoo "Louisiana Voodoo") practitioner [Marie Laveau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Laveau "Marie Laveau"), but bailed themselves out of jail and skipped their court date to drive to their next performance in Florida. Following the tour they released seven songs from the November 1981 performance in San Francisco in limited numbers only to members of the Fiend Club as the _[Evilive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evilive "Evilive")_ EP.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

By this time Danzig was growing increasingly dissatisfied with the Misfits and had begun writing songs for a new band project. In June 1983 he confided to [Henry Rollins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Rollins "Henry Rollins") that he planned to quit the group.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-coley-10) In July 1983 the Misfits finished recording their EP, and Danzig decided to record two more songs that he had intended for his new project, turning it into a full album. _[Earth A.D./Wolfs Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_A.D./Wolfs\_Blood "Earth A.D./Wolfs Blood")_ demonstrated the increased influence of [hardcore punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_punk "Hardcore punk") and [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") on the band, though they would break up just two months before it was released. After a series of arguments with Danzig, Robo left the band in August and Danzig became further disenchanted, beginning to audition musicians for his next project.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

On October 29, 1983, the Misfits played their annual [Halloween](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halloween "Halloween") performance at Greystone Hall in Detroit with the Necros. Danzig had selected Brian Damage (real name Brian Keats), formerly of [Genöcide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen%C3%B6cide "Genöcide") and [Verbal Abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verbal_Abuse "Verbal Abuse"), as the band's new drummer. However, Damage became [drunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drunkenness "Drunkenness") before the show and could not play properly. After several songs Doyle escorted him off the stage and Todd Swalla of _The Necros_ filled in for the remainder of the performance. Tensions came to a head and Danzig announced to the audience that it would be the band's final show. Upon returning to Lodi the band members went their separate ways.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### 1984–1995: New projects and legal battles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1984–1995: New projects and legal battles")]

Following the breakup of the Misfits, Danzig launched his new band [Samhain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samhain_(band) "Samhain (band)"), moving away from [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock"), and toward more experimental [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") with a grim atmosphere. Several Misfits songs were rerecorded for Samhain albums, including "Horror Business" (as "Horror Biz"), "All Hell Breaks Loose" (as "All Hell"), and "Halloween II". In 1986, the band signed to a major record label and Danzig replaced most of the [rhythm section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_section "Rhythm section"), renaming the group [Danzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danzig_(band) "Danzig (band)"). He continues to front Danzig, who have released ten albums ranging in style from [blues rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues_rock "Blues rock")-influenced heavy metal to [industrial rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_rock "Industrial rock"), and has also released two solo albums.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Jerry Only and Doyle, meanwhile, moved to [Vernon, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vernon_Township,_New_Jersey "Vernon Township, New Jersey") to work at their father's machine parts factory full-time. Jerry Only had married and had a daughter and became more serious about his Christian faith, regretting some of the things he had done with the Misfits. In 1987, he and Doyle formed the short-lived [Kryst the Conqueror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kryst_the_Conqueror "Kryst the Conqueror"), a [Christian heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_heavy_metal "Christian heavy metal") band with barbarian imagery.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Although the Misfits' popularity did not extend beyond the underground punk scene during their six years of activity, public interest in the band increased in the years following their breakup. The success of Danzig's post-Misfits' work led to interest in his past work, and several high-profile rock bands professed fondness for the Misfits. Most notably, [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica")[covered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") the Misfits songs "[Last Caress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Caress "Last Caress")" and "[Green Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Hell_(song) "Green Hell (song)")" on _[The $5.98 E.P. - Garage Days Re-Revisited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_$5.98\_E.P.\_-\_Garage\_Days\_Re-Revisited "The $5.98 E.P. - Garage Days Re-Revisited")_ (1987), and [Guns N' Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_N'_Roses "Guns N' Roses") covered "[Attitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attitude_(Misfits_song) "Attitude (Misfits song)")" on _["The Spaghetti Incident?"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%22The\_Spaghetti\_Incident%3F%22 "\"The Spaghetti Incident?\"")_ (1993). Several albums of reissued and previously unreleased Misfits material were issued between 1985 and 1987, the first being the [compilation album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album")_[Legacy of Brutality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legacy\_of\_Brutality "Legacy of Brutality")_ (1985) which included many of the songs from the unreleased _[Static Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Static\_Age "Static Age")_ album. Danzig [overdubbed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overdubbing "Overdubbing") many of the album's instrument tracks to avoid having to pay [royalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royalties "Royalties") to the other former band members. _[Misfits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collection\_I "Collection I")_, more commonly referred to as _Collection I_, followed in 1986. The _[Evilive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evilive "Evilive")_ EP was reissued as a full album in 1987 with five additional tracks.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Only contacted Danzig about receiving a portion of the royalties from these albums' sales, beginning a legal battle that lasted several years and involved other past members of the band. All of the Misfits material had been credited to Danzig, and though Only later conceded that Danzig had written nearly all of the lyrics and most of the music, he contended that he and Doyle "wrote 25% or maybe 30% of the music"[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-11) and deserved compensation. Danzig, however, insisted that he had written all of the songs in their entirety and that the other members' creative input had been minimal. Eventually Only ceased his pursuit of songwriting credits and sought the rights to use the Misfits name and imagery, including the now-famous "Crimson Ghost" skull face logo.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1995, the parties reached an out-of-court settlement that allowed Only and Doyle to record and perform as the Misfits, sharing merchandising rights with Danzig. _[Collection II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collection\_II "Collection II")_, a third compilation of Misfits songs, was released later that year.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### 1995–2000: Reformation and new lineup

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1995–2000: Reformation and new lineup")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Misfits_%28Michael_Graves%29.gif/250px-Misfits_%28Michael_Graves%29.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Misfits_(Michael_Graves).gif)

Misfits performing live in 1998

Only and Doyle immediately set about reforming the Misfits, bringing in drummer [David Calabrese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Chud "Dr. Chud"), also known as Dr. Chud, who had worked with them in Kryst the Conqueror. Glenn Danzig refused to return as the band's lead singer. [Dave Vanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Vanian "Dave Vanian") of [The Damned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Damned_(band) "The Damned (band)") was also approached but declined. The band, now reformed with one original founding member, Jerry Only, held open auditions for a new vocalist. Nineteen-year-old singer [Michael Emanuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michale_Graves "Michale Graves") had recently recorded a demo tape in hopes of starting a music career, and the owner of the recording studio suggested that he audition for the Misfits. Being unfamiliar with the band, Emanuel listened to _Collection I_ on a [walkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkman "Walkman") to learn the lyrics and melodies while working his job as a greenskeeper. He impressed the band with his audition and was accepted as the new lead singer under the pseudonym Michale Graves, while Doyle adopted the new stage full name Doyle Wolfgang von Frankenstein. The new lineup made an appearance in the 1995 film _[Animal Room](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal\_Room "Animal Room")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1996, [_The Misfits_ coffin box set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Misfits_(album) "The Misfits (album)") was released, containing nearly all of the band's Danzig-era material recorded from 1977 to 1983 (with the exception of _[Walk Among Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk\_Among\_Us "Walk Among Us")_). The set included the incomplete fourteen-song _Static Age_ album, released for the first time in its entirety on CD, as well as the overdubbed and alternate versions of songs that had previously been released on _Legacy of Brutality_, _Collection I_, and _Collection II_. _Static Age_ was also released as a separate album the following year, including all seventeen tracks that had been recorded during the January 1978 sessions. The release of the box set and _Static Age_ made the Misfits' complete early catalog widely available for the first time.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

A [tribute album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribute_album "Tribute album") was also released in 1997 titled _[Violent World: A Tribute to the Misfits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violent\_World:\_A\_Tribute\_to\_the\_Misfits "Violent World: A Tribute to the Misfits")_, featuring numerous [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") and [hardcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_punk "Hardcore punk") bands covering their songs. Another tribute album, _[Hell on Earth: A Tribute to the Misfits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell\_on\_Earth:\_A\_Tribute\_to\_the\_Misfits "Hell on Earth: A Tribute to the Misfits")_, was released in 2000 featuring [death metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_metal "Death metal"), [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock"), and [gothic rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_rock "Gothic rock") acts.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The new incarnation of the Misfits released their debut album _[American Psycho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Psycho\_(album) "American Psycho (album)")_ in 1997.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-PM-12) They filmed music videos for the songs "American Psycho" and "[Dig Up Her Bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dig_Up_Her_Bones "Dig Up Her Bones")". The band toured Europe and North America in support of the album and appeared as characters in [World Championship Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Championship_Wrestling "World Championship Wrestling") as tag team for wrestler [Ian "Vampiro" Hodgkinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampiro "Vampiro").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-13) Graves took a hiatus from the band in 1998, during which Myke Itzazone of [Empire Hideous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_Hideous "Empire Hideous") filled in as singer during tours of South America and Europe. After Graves' return the band signed to [Roadrunner Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roadrunner_Records "Roadrunner Records"), releasing _[Famous Monsters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famous\_Monsters "Famous Monsters")_ in October 1999 and filming a music video for the single _[Scream!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scream!\_(Misfits\_song) "Scream! (Misfits song)")_ They made additional film appearances in _[Big Money Hustlas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big\_Money\_Hustlas "Big Money Hustlas")_ (2000), _[Bruiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruiser\_(2000\_film) "Bruiser (2000 film)")_ (2000), and _Campfire Stories_ (2001) and continued to tour, but tensions between the band members began to grow. During a performance at the [House of Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Blues "House of Blues") in [Orlando, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando,_Florida "Orlando, Florida") on October 25, 2000, Graves and Chud both quit the band and walked off stage. The two later released an album under the name [Graves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graves_(band) "Graves (band)") before splitting up; Graves went on to sing for [Gotham Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gotham_Road "Gotham Road") and then launched a solo career, while Chud formed [Dr. Chud's X-Ward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Chud's_X-Ward "Dr. Chud's X-Ward"). Meanwhile, Doyle took an indefinite hiatus from performing as he divorced, remarried, had a fourth child, and dealt with [tendonitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendonitis "Tendonitis") in his elbow.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### 2001–2008: 25th anniversary and all-star lineup

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2001–2008: 25th anniversary and all-star lineup")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Jerry_Only_live_with_the_Misifts%2C_Sala_Copernico%2C_Madrid%2C_2008-04-23_%283%29.jpg/250px-Jerry_Only_live_with_the_Misifts%2C_Sala_Copernico%2C_Madrid%2C_2008-04-23_%283%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jerry_Only_live_with_the_Misifts,_Sala_Copernico,_Madrid,_2008-04-23_(3).jpg)

After the departure of the other band members, bassist [Jerry Only](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Only "Jerry Only") took over as singer and recruited veteran [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") musicians to continue the band.

As the sole remaining founding member of the Misfits, Jerry Only took over lead vocal duties in addition to playing bass guitar and recruited veteran musicians [Dez Cadena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dez_Cadena "Dez Cadena"), former guitarist and vocalist for [Black Flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Flag_(band) "Black Flag (band)"), an idea Doyle was not fond of, leading him to quit. Also [Marky Ramone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marky_Ramone "Marky Ramone"), former drummer of the [Ramones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramones "Ramones"), joined for a Misfits 25th anniversary tour which lasted intermittently for nearly three years. Former Black Flag and Misfits drummer [Robo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robo_(musician) "Robo (musician)") filled in for Ramone during some stretches of the tour. Only released _[Cuts from the Crypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuts\_from\_the\_Crypt "Cuts from the Crypt")_ in 2001, a compilation of demos and rarities covering the band's period with Graves and Chud from 1995 to 2001. This fulfilled the band's contractual obligations to Roadrunner Records, whom Only had grown dissatisfied with.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Also in 2001 [Caroline Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caroline_Records "Caroline Records") announced that they would release recordings from the Misfits' August 1980 album sessions as _[12 Hits from Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12\_Hits\_from\_Hell "12 Hits from Hell")_. However, both Only and [Glenn Danzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Danzig "Glenn Danzig") abruptly called off production of the album, citing concerns with the mixing, mastering, layout, and packaging.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Only and longtime collaborator [John Cafiero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cafiero "John Cafiero") soon launched their own label, [Misfits Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_Records "Misfits Records"), and released [a split single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Open_'til_It's_Doomsday "Don't Open 'til It's Doomsday") featuring the Misfits and Japanese [horror punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_punk "Horror punk") band [Balzac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balzac_(band) "Balzac (band)"). The Only/Cadena/Ramone lineup of the Misfits released the covers album _[Project 1950](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project\_1950 "Project 1950")_ in 2003, performing renditions of classic [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") songs from the 1950s and 1960s. The album featured guest appearances from [Ronnie Spector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_Spector "Ronnie Spector"), [Jimmy Destri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Destri "Jimmy Destri"), [Ed Manion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Manion "Ed Manion"), and [John Cafiero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cafiero "John Cafiero"). The band toured intermittently in support of the album until 2005, when Ramone left the band and was replaced by Robo. They booked a full European tour that year, but problems with Robo's [visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_(document) "Visa (document)") led to the cancellation of all dates in the United Kingdom. A rescheduled UK tour followed in September.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Doyle_Wolfgang_von_Frankenstein.jpg/250px-Doyle_Wolfgang_von_Frankenstein.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Doyle_Wolfgang_von_Frankenstein.jpg)

Starting in 2004, [Doyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doyle_Wolfgang_von_Frankenstein "Doyle Wolfgang von Frankenstein") joined [Danzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danzig_(band) "Danzig (band)") onstage to perform half-hour sets of early Misfits songs.

Doyle had meanwhile reunited with Glenn Danzig, joining [Danzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danzig_(band) "Danzig (band)") onstage during performances in December 2004 to play guitar for 30-minute sets of old Misfits songs midway through the band's setlist. It was the first time the two had performed together in over twenty years, and the first time Doyle had performed since his hiatus. Danzig called the performances "the closest thing to a Misfits reunion anyone is ever going to see".[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-14) These sets featuring Doyle continued through Danzig's 2005 _Blackest of the Black_ tour and 2006 Australian tour. Glenn Danzig had announced his intention to retire from touring following these, though he later contradicted this by announcing a Danzig 20th anniversary tour in 2008.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-15) In 2007, he produced Doyle's new project [Gorgeous Frankenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorgeous_Frankenstein "Gorgeous Frankenstein"). Doyle later indicated that plans had been in place for the Misfits to reunite with Glenn Danzig beginning in 2002, but that Jerry Only and his manager had "put a fuckin' monkey wrench in it."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-16)

### 2009–2015: 30th anniversary and new albums

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2009–2015: 30th anniversary and new albums")]

In 2009 and 2010, the Misfits performed an extended 30th anniversary world tour. A new single, "[Land of the Dead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_of_the_Dead_(Misfits_song) "Land of the Dead (Misfits song)")" was released October 27, 2009, marking the band's first release of new studio material in six years and the only release by the lineup of Only, Cadena, and Robo.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-17) Robo was dismissed from the band in 2010, with Only explaining that ongoing problems with his Colombian passport inhibited the band's ability to tour consistently.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-Blair_1-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-punknews_11-24-10-19) He was replaced by Eric "Chupacabra" Arce of [Murphy's Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murphy's_Law_(band) "Murphy's Law (band)"), who had previously filled in with the band for tours in 2000 and 2001.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-Blair_1-18) The Only/Cadena/Arce lineup released a new album, _[The Devil's Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Devil's\_Rain\_(album) "The Devil's Rain (album)")_, recorded with producer [Ed Stasium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Stasium "Ed Stasium") and titled after [the 1975 film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Devil's_Rain_(film) "The Devil's Rain (film)") starring [William Shatner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shatner "William Shatner").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-Blair_1-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-punknews_11-24-10-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-Blair_2-20) The album was released on October 4, 2011.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-21) During the latter quarter of 2011, former vocalist Danzig and guitarist Doyle performed Misfits songs on four occasions as part of the Danzig _Legacy_ tour. The first of the four shows, which took place on October 7 in Chicago, saw a sold-out crowd.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-22)

In 2013, the Misfits released their third live album, _[Dead Alive!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead\_Alive! "Dead Alive!")_. In October, they released a 12" single fronted by a new recording of "Descending Angel", backed by a cover of "[Science Fiction/Double Feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_Fiction/Double_Feature "Science Fiction/Double Feature")", a song they previously only played live. Meanwhile, Danzig and Doyle continued to regularly play Misfits songs and included a set on Danzig's 25th anniversary tour.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-24) In October 2013, publisher [Rowman & Littlefield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowman_&_Littlefield "Rowman & Littlefield") published _This Music Leaves Stains_ by James Greene, an unofficial Misfits biography, which tells the story of each incarnation of the band as well as spin-off projects such as [Samhain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samhain_(band) "Samhain (band)") and [Danzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danzig_(band) "Danzig (band)").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In late 2015, the Misfits released the songs "Vampire Girl" and "Zombie Girl" as a single.

### 2016–present: Reunion as the Original Misfits

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2016–present: Reunion as the Original Misfits")]

In May 2016, Danzig, Only, and Doyle announced that they would perform together for the first time in 33 years, under the name The Original Misfits.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-26) Only told _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ that the reunion stemmed from a legal discussion that "was turning into another court battle and it turned into a reunion."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-27) Court documents show that Danzig and Only discussed a reunion as part of settlement negotiations as early as 2014.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-28) In June of that year, the Misfits released the _Friday the 13th_ EP featuring material written by Only with his son Jerry Other on guitar and Chupacabra on drums.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-newsletter-29) In September the Misfits lineup of Danzig, Only and Doyle, along with guitarist [Acey Slade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acey_Slade "Acey Slade") and drummer [Dave Lombardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Lombardo "Dave Lombardo"), headlined their two reunion shows, performing 25-song sets at the [Riot Fest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riot_Fest "Riot Fest") in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") and [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver").

In an interview with _Rolling Stone_ following the first reunion show Only was asked about the future of the Misfits, and if there were plans to continue and possibly record new music. "I want it to continue. I know Doyle wants it to continue. I know Glenn wants it to continue. We just have to be big-enough people to make it continue. And that's where we're at. Whatever it takes. We're going into our 40th anniversary so the timing couldn't be more perfect. Eventually Doyle's got to write a new album; I've got to write a new album; Glenn's got to write a new album. Why don't we work together and make the greatest album ever? Now we've got different elements. We've got Doyle playing more of a metal kind of thing. We've got Dave, who we're trying to figure out what the fuck he's doing. And Glenn's got his own thing. And Acey (Slade, second guitar) fills in good, too. And I've got the band where it is today. So it's a matter of re-molding and using all the different elements that I've got." When asked if Danzig would want to record new music Only said, "I think it's got to evolve naturally. The thing is we've tried to plan things, and then we stand there and wait, and as it comes we'll just do it. When we go back – I don't know about Glenn – but I canceled our touring and everything for this, so I'm going to go home and write and lift."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-Blabbermouth-30)

In December 2017, the reunited lineup performed two concerts at the [MGM Grand Garden Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGM_Grand_Garden_Arena "MGM Grand Garden Arena") in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas") and [The Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Forum_(Inglewood,_California) "The Forum (Inglewood, California)") in [Inglewood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood,_California "Inglewood, California").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-31) In 2018, the band played at the [Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Center "Prudential Center") in [Newark, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newark,_New_Jersey "Newark, New Jersey") and in 2019 at the [Allstate Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allstate_Arena "Allstate Arena") in suburban Chicago.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-vanyaland.com-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-NJ.com-33) In a June 2019 interview, Danzig indicated that the reunion period might be drawing to a close, saying that, "We're not gonna do many more."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-34) The news from Danzig came on the heels of an in-depth article from [MetalSucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetalSucks "MetalSucks") analyzing legal documents related to the original reunion planning that revealed other details, including the statement, "The parties agree to perform no fewer than ten Misfits reunion shows to coincide with the 40th anniversary of the band."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-35) Despite Danzig's pessimism, it was announced that same month that the Original Misfits would be replacing [Megadeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megadeth "Megadeth") at the Psycho Las Vegas event in August due to [Dave Mustaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Mustaine "Dave Mustaine")'s throat cancer diagnosis. Following the Las Vegas show, the reunited lineup was booked for concerts at the [Fiddler's Green Amphitheatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiddler's_Green_Amphitheatre "Fiddler's Green Amphitheatre") in [Greenwood Village, Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwood_Village,_Colorado "Greenwood Village, Colorado"), at the [Oracle Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oracle_Arena "Oracle Arena") in [Oakland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland,_California "Oakland, California"), at [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle")'s [White River Amphitheatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_River_Amphitheatre "White River Amphitheatre"), at New York's [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden"), at [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia")'s [Wells Fargo Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wells_Fargo_Center_(Philadelphia) "Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)") and at [Discovery Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discovery_Park_(Sacramento) "Discovery Park (Sacramento)") in Sacramento.

In May 2021, it was announced that the Original Misfits would play [Riot Fest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riot_Fest "Riot Fest") as co-headliners with [My Chemical Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Chemical_Romance "My Chemical Romance") alongside [Nine Inch Nails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_Inch_Nails "Nine Inch Nails").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-36)

In August 2022, they announced an Original Misfits lineup would perform its second headlining show of 2022 on Halloween weekend in Dallas, at Dos Equis Pavilion on October 29, with special guests [Alice Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Cooper "Alice Cooper") and [FEAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear_(band) "Fear (band)").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-37)

Original Misfits drummer Manny Martinez died on December 16, 2023, aged 69.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-38)

In November 2024, it was announced that the Original Misfits would perform at [Coachella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella "Coachella") on April 12 and April 19, 2025. The band was listed on the official tour poster with their original font logo.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-39)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Artistry")]

### Musical style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Musical style")]

Each incarnation of the Misfits has made use of [horror film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film") and [science fiction film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_film "Science fiction film")-inspired themes and imagery, with makeup, clothing, artwork, and lyrics drawn from [B movies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B_movie "B movie") and television serials, many from the 1950s through 1970s. Musically the band are often recognized as progenitors of the [horror punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_punk "Horror punk"), [psychobilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychobilly "Psychobilly") and [punk metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_metal "Punk metal") subgenres and have drawn from [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock"), heavy metal, and 1950s [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") and [rockabilly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockabilly "Rockabilly") to inform their style.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-40)_[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ describes them as "the archetypal horror-punk band of the late 1970s and early '80s",[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-RS1-41) and they are considered icons in punk music and culture.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-POTPLAN-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-iron-43) The Misfits have also been described as [pop-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_punk "Pop punk").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-46)

The early incarnations of the Misfits are associated with the [hardcore punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_punk "Hardcore punk") movement of the early 1980s, though _[American Hardcore: A Tribal History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Hardcore:\_A\_Tribal\_History "American Hardcore: A Tribal History")_ author [Steven Blush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Blush "Steven Blush") notes that "though crucial to the rise of hardcore, [they] were in fact in a league of their own...The Misfits delivered a hyper-yet-melodic assault based in 50/60s-style rock, taking the [Buddy Holly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Holly "Buddy Holly")/[Gene Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Vincent "Gene Vincent") foundation and making it nuclear."[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-47) Jon de Rosa of [Pitchfork Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_Media "Pitchfork Media") describes how the band's sound was different from the punk rock coming out of New York at the time: "New York punk was just punk, simple and static. When Glenn started the Misfits, he mutated the punk sound and image into something darker and more sinister, a punk-metal hybrid that later found bloom in the [quiet, boring suburbs of Oslo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Metal "Black Metal") and the [boggy backwaters surrounding Tampa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_metal "Death metal"). Punk belonged to the media/celebrity hubs of London and New York. Ghoul rock was for the kids in the suburbs where nothing ever happens".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-48)

Andy Weller of the [Necros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necros "Necros") recalls the band's transition from traditional punk rock in the late 1970s to hardcore in the early 1980s: "(You) could hear it on the records. It went from this [Ramones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramones "Ramones")-type stuff, to nine months later, where they put out records that were so fast it's unreal."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-49) By the recording of _[Earth A.D./Wolfs Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_A.D./Wolfs\_Blood "Earth A.D./Wolfs Blood")_ the band were playing faster, more aggressive material. According to Blush, "The Misfits' strengths as a hardcore group lay in non-[hardcore] attributes–melodic songs and larger-than-life-aura–but by the time of _Earth AD_ Glenn was writing hyperspeed blasts that sounded very standard."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-50)

The new version of the Misfits launched by Jerry Only and Doyle in the 1990s, kept the horror punk themes, but went in a more [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") direction with blasting drums and crunchy guitars.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-punknews-51) Reviewing _[American Psycho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Psycho\_(album) "American Psycho (album)")_, Stephen Erlewine of [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") called the new incarnation "a kitschy goth-punk outfit that relies more on metal than hardcore",[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-erlewine-52) while _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ remarked that the band's new style blended "some old-style punk, a little metal and an occasional all-out thrasher."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-53) Greg Prato, reviewing the 2001 album _[Cuts from the Crypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuts\_from\_the\_Crypt "Cuts from the Crypt")_, noted that "the latter-day Misfits are much more heavy metal based than in their earlier work – as their punk roots have all but been erased."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-54)

### Devilock

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Devilock")]

Main article: [Devilock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devilock "Devilock")

The devilock is a [hairstyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hairstyle "Hairstyle") created by Misfits in the late 1970s.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-55) In a devilock, the sides and back of the hair are kept short, while the front is kept long and combed forward.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-56)

In an early 1980s interview, Jerry Only claimed that the devilock was based on a "tidal wave" hairstyle seen among the 1970s [skateboarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skateboarding "Skateboarding") communities. In the same interview, former Misfits vocalist [Glenn Danzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Danzig "Glenn Danzig") explains that his version of the hairstyle developed from an imitation of [Eddie Munster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Munster "Eddie Munster")'s hairstyle. A style similar to the Devilock was sported earlier - for instance the elephant trunk hairstyle of the 1950s, the Surfari's cover picture of 'Gum-dipped Slicks' (1964) shows a member of the band with a devilock-like quiff,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-57) as did the guitarist from the contemporaneous Tornadoes of Bustin' Surfboards fame.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-58)

### Logo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Logo")]

The Misfits skull logo has been listed among the best band logos from publications such as _[Loudwire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudwire "Loudwire")_.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-59) The logo has been referred to as both "the fiend," and "the crimson ghost."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-:0-60)[Glenn Danzig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Danzig "Glenn Danzig") took the image from the face of the titular ghoul character of the 1946 film _[The Crimson Ghost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crimson\_Ghost "The Crimson Ghost")._[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-61) It first appeared on their single "Horror Business" in 1979. Though Danzig had no idea the logo would become as iconic as it did, it fittingly represents everything that the band stands for, and so was adopted as the band's signature image.

In 2014, Glenn Danzig sued bassist [Jerry Only](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Only "Jerry Only") for multiple violations, involving the misuse of Misfits trademarks and logos when Only had formed a new version of the Misfits without Danzig. The complaint included multiple references to Only's use of the skull. In 2020, another lawsuit involving the logo was filed by the Misfits against Abrams Books, the publisher of the 2019 visual history book _Scream With Me: The Enduring Legacy of the Misfits_. However the lawsuit was reportedly dropped five months later _._[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-:0-60)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Misfits_(band)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Having been described as "the very model of an influential punk band" by Tim Stegall of [_Alternative Press_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_Press_(magazine) "Alternative Press (magazine)"), the Misfits have had a large influence on numerous bands in the [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") and [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") genres.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-62) Acts such as [Megadeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megadeth "Megadeth"),[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-63)[Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica"), [Guns N' Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_N'_Roses "Guns N' Roses"), [Marilyn Manson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Manson_(band) "Marilyn Manson (band)"), [Green Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Day "Green Day"), [the Offspring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Offspring "The Offspring"), [NOFX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOFX "NOFX"), [AFI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFI_(band) "AFI (band)"), [Avenged Sevenfold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avenged_Sevenfold "Avenged Sevenfold"), [My Chemical Romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Chemical_Romance "My Chemical Romance") and [Cradle of Filth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cradle_of_Filth "Cradle of Filth") have also listed the band as an influence.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-:1-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-:2-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-:3-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-:4-4)[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone") ranked their 1986 [self titled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(Misfits_album) "Misfits (Misfits album)") compilation album as the 35th greatest punk album of all time,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-64) whilst _[Revolver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolver\_(magazine) "Revolver (magazine)")_ ranked _[Walk Among Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk\_Among\_Us "Walk Among Us")_ the 9th greatest punk album.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-65) Their sound and logo which comes from the 1946 film _[The Crimson Ghost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crimson\_Ghost "The Crimson Ghost")_ has also been described as "one of the most powerful sounds and images of the punk era."[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-66)

In 2021 the staff of [_Consequence_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consequence_(website) "Consequence (website)") ranked Misfits as the 9th greatest punk band of all time stating "Yet with songs about zombies, gore, and ghoulish imagery, Misfits integrated a sense of fantasy into the scene. They gave punk permission to be escapist and dark, and coupled this with catchy scores that bursted with snarl — a clear indicator that the quintessential punk attitude was never lost despite their different lyrical approach."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-67) In 2023 [Ultimate Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultimate_Guitar "Ultimate Guitar") listed the group among their 10 essential [horror punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_punk "Horror punk") bands writing "The genre's OGs and arguably still the most successful act to come out of horror punk, even almost 50 years since their inception; The Misfits continue to embody everything great about this style."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-68)

Due to the limited quantities of the bands original singles and albums they have become a [collectors item](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collectable "Collectable") and have regularly sold for thousands of dollars and routinely appear on the most valuable lists on sites such as [Discogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discogs "Discogs").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misfits_(band)#cite_note-70)

# Give Your Scalp a Little Extra Attention

## The hair on our heads is just about the only thing not covered by a face mask these days. Here’s how to protect the skin on your head and keep your tresses shining

Written by Natasha Wolff  

[View the gallery](https://dujour.com/gallery/scalp-treatments-hair-products/)

[![Image 61](https://b4067926.assetcdn.net/4067926/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/78c6671247a9-200x240.jpg?lossy=0&strip=1&webp=1)](https://dujour.com/gallery/scalp-treatments-hair-products/)

We often forget that scalp is skin. We can’t see it, but indeed it is just as important as the skin on our faces and bodies. Now, skincare-grade ingredients are finally being added to haircare products for some scalp detox.

“Seasonal changes can always affect our skin, and the sweat, humidity and heat that summer brings with it can create a moist, warm environment on your scalp in which microbes, the bacteria that causes dandruff and irritation, thrive,” says[Dr. Barbara Sturm](https://dujour.com/beauty/spend-a-day-with-dr-barbara-sturm-molecular-cosmetics-skincare/). It’s important to note the positive effects a healthy scalp can have on hair’s strength, texture and appearance. “Hair that’s grown from an unhealthy scalp shows signs of roughness or breakage and in some cases, shine reduction, dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis or psoriasis.”

Months spent swimming in a chlorinated pool or in salty ocean water can be harsh on the hair and scalp, so your scalp needs more TLC. “Fall is a good time to reset and develop a consistent haircare routine to repair the damage to our tresses and encourage stronger hair growth,” says Fable & Mane’s co-founder, Akash Mehta, a vegan, plant-based hair wellness line inspired by ancient Indian beauty secrets. The brand’s products feature ingredients like centella asiatica and adaptogenic ashwagandha to help the scalp microbiome adapt to changes in environment, internal hormonal changes and stress. Exfoliating the scalp is crucial to removing buildup and toxins from color treatments and styling products. “A balanced scalp microbiome is key for healthy hair,” says the brand’s other co-founder Nikita Mehta. Using products with silicone also causes damage to hair, so exfoliating the scalp should be done weekly to reboot the scalp. “Talking about the scalp wasn’t a sexy subject before but now people are much more open to discussing the details,” says Helen Reavey, a trichologist and founder of hair and scalp care brand [Act+Acre](https://actandacre.com/collections/all-products). “Now scalp care is part of the conversation.” Act+Acre’s products, like its Scalp Renew, Scalp Detox and Stem Cell Serum, treat the scalp like your skin cleansing and exfoliating while leaving all the good bacteria.

Robbie Salter co-created[Jupiter](https://hellojupiter.com/), a line of shampoos, conditioners and repair products to address dandruff and dry scalp. “While the summer has its share of scalp damaging moments, the winter is often your scalp’s worst enemy,” Salter explains. “We tend to go longer in between washes, wear hats to stave off the cold or hide a little greasy buildup—each creating a breeding ground for oil and fungal buildup. Look to gentle formulations with medicated ingredients to not only target those issues at the source, but to establish the strongest foundation for healthy hair growth.” Jupiter is the only salon-quality dual system scalp repair company to offer both a line for those treating dandruff and, with the launch of its new dry scalp focus system, dry scalp.

After achieving success with her skincare line[Drunk Elephant](https://dujour.com/cities/houston/drunk-elephant-new-hair-body-products-tiffany-masterson-interview/), it was only a matter of time before the brand’s founder and CEO, Tiffany Masterson, tackled the scalp with a new line of fragrance- and sulfate-free shampoo, conditioner and styling products. “You can’t have good hair without a healthy scalp,” says Masterson, whose son and husband both struggle with long-term scalp issues. “It’s super important to exfoliate weekly to have a clean and healthy scalp.” Drunk Elephant’s T.L.C. Happi Scalp Scrub has both physical (plant cellulose beads) and chemical exfoliation in the form of AHAs (alpha hydroxy acids, such as glycolic or lactic acids) and BHAs (beta hydroxy acid, like salicylic acid). “Traditionally, haircare products have contained all sorts of ingredients, like silicones, that could disrupt the health of the scalp and cause buildup,” Masterson explains. “Our biocompatible line focuses on healthy pH levels, formulations the skin recognizes, small molecular structure that’s easily absorbed and effective active ingredients.”

“Your diet is also so important because your hair needs certain vitamins and minerals to be healthy and if the hair doesn’t have them at the birth stage it can weaken the hair,” says Reavey. “Your hair is the last to get nutrients, so you need to have a healthy surplus of vitamins and minerals in your body.” Act+Acre’s new[Plant Based Hair Capsules](https://actandacre.com/products/plant-based-hair-capsules) help provide all the nutrients your hair needs outside of your diet.

Entrepreneur Nancy Twine founded plant-powered, vegan haircare line[Briogeo](https://dujour.com/gallery/emergency-deskside-beauty-essentials/#slide-4) to fix damaged locks. “I can see how the scalp can be overlooked—traditionally, we are accustomed to cleansing and conditioning just our hair,” says Twine. “This is why I created Briogeo’s Scalp Revival Charcoal + Coconut Oil Micro-Exfoliating Shampoo. It is formulated with plant-based exfoliators that gently remove buildup from the scalp and coconut oil that moisturizes to help prevent a dry, flaky scalp.” She also recommends using a scalp exfoliator once or twice a week like her Charcoal + Tea Tree Scalp Treatment, which is included in the brand’s Scalp Revival product set and features detoxifying Binchotan charcoal that draws out impurities from the scalp. “This formulation contains a cooling blend of tea tree, peppermint and spearmint oils that help reduce itchiness, irritation and inflammation,” she says.

# Give Your Scalp a Little Extra Attention

## The hair on our heads is just about the only thing not covered by a face mask these days. Here’s how to protect the skin on your head and keep your tresses shining

Written by Natasha Wolff  

[View the gallery](https://dujour.com/gallery/scalp-treatments-hair-products/)

[![Image 61](https://b4067926.assetcdn.net/4067926/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/78c6671247a9-200x240.jpg?lossy=0&strip=1&webp=1)](https://dujour.com/gallery/scalp-treatments-hair-products/)

We often forget that scalp is skin. We can’t see it, but indeed it is just as important as the skin on our faces and bodies. Now, skincare-grade ingredients are finally being added to haircare products for some scalp detox.

“Seasonal changes can always affect our skin, and the sweat, humidity and heat that summer brings with it can create a moist, warm environment on your scalp in which microbes, the bacteria that causes dandruff and irritation, thrive,” says[Dr. Barbara Sturm](https://dujour.com/beauty/spend-a-day-with-dr-barbara-sturm-molecular-cosmetics-skincare/). It’s important to note the positive effects a healthy scalp can have on hair’s strength, texture and appearance. “Hair that’s grown from an unhealthy scalp shows signs of roughness or breakage and in some cases, shine reduction, dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis or psoriasis.”

Months spent swimming in a chlorinated pool or in salty ocean water can be harsh on the hair and scalp, so your scalp needs more TLC. “Fall is a good time to reset and develop a consistent haircare routine to repair the damage to our tresses and encourage stronger hair growth,” says Fable & Mane’s co-founder, Akash Mehta, a vegan, plant-based hair wellness line inspired by ancient Indian beauty secrets. The brand’s products feature ingredients like centella asiatica and adaptogenic ashwagandha to help the scalp microbiome adapt to changes in environment, internal hormonal changes and stress. Exfoliating the scalp is crucial to removing buildup and toxins from color treatments and styling products. “A balanced scalp microbiome is key for healthy hair,” says the brand’s other co-founder Nikita Mehta. Using products with silicone also causes damage to hair, so exfoliating the scalp should be done weekly to reboot the scalp. “Talking about the scalp wasn’t a sexy subject before but now people are much more open to discussing the details,” says Helen Reavey, a trichologist and founder of hair and scalp care brand [Act+Acre](https://actandacre.com/collections/all-products). “Now scalp care is part of the conversation.” Act+Acre’s products, like its Scalp Renew, Scalp Detox and Stem Cell Serum, treat the scalp like your skin cleansing and exfoliating while leaving all the good bacteria.

Robbie Salter co-created[Jupiter](https://hellojupiter.com/), a line of shampoos, conditioners and repair products to address dandruff and dry scalp. “While the summer has its share of scalp damaging moments, the winter is often your scalp’s worst enemy,” Salter explains. “We tend to go longer in between washes, wear hats to stave off the cold or hide a little greasy buildup—each creating a breeding ground for oil and fungal buildup. Look to gentle formulations with medicated ingredients to not only target those issues at the source, but to establish the strongest foundation for healthy hair growth.” Jupiter is the only salon-quality dual system scalp repair company to offer both a line for those treating dandruff and, with the launch of its new dry scalp focus system, dry scalp.

After achieving success with her skincare line[Drunk Elephant](https://dujour.com/cities/houston/drunk-elephant-new-hair-body-products-tiffany-masterson-interview/), it was only a matter of time before the brand’s founder and CEO, Tiffany Masterson, tackled the scalp with a new line of fragrance- and sulfate-free shampoo, conditioner and styling products. “You can’t have good hair without a healthy scalp,” says Masterson, whose son and husband both struggle with long-term scalp issues. “It’s super important to exfoliate weekly to have a clean and healthy scalp.” Drunk Elephant’s T.L.C. Happi Scalp Scrub has both physical (plant cellulose beads) and chemical exfoliation in the form of AHAs (alpha hydroxy acids, such as glycolic or lactic acids) and BHAs (beta hydroxy acid, like salicylic acid). “Traditionally, haircare products have contained all sorts of ingredients, like silicones, that could disrupt the health of the scalp and cause buildup,” Masterson explains. “Our biocompatible line focuses on healthy pH levels, formulations the skin recognizes, small molecular structure that’s easily absorbed and effective active ingredients.”

“Your diet is also so important because your hair needs certain vitamins and minerals to be healthy and if the hair doesn’t have them at the birth stage it can weaken the hair,” says Reavey. “Your hair is the last to get nutrients, so you need to have a healthy surplus of vitamins and minerals in your body.” Act+Acre’s new[Plant Based Hair Capsules](https://actandacre.com/products/plant-based-hair-capsules) help provide all the nutrients your hair needs outside of your diet.

Entrepreneur Nancy Twine founded plant-powered, vegan haircare line[Briogeo](https://dujour.com/gallery/emergency-deskside-beauty-essentials/#slide-4) to fix damaged locks. “I can see how the scalp can be overlooked—traditionally, we are accustomed to cleansing and conditioning just our hair,” says Twine. “This is why I created Briogeo’s Scalp Revival Charcoal + Coconut Oil Micro-Exfoliating Shampoo. It is formulated with plant-based exfoliators that gently remove buildup from the scalp and coconut oil that moisturizes to help prevent a dry, flaky scalp.” She also recommends using a scalp exfoliator once or twice a week like her Charcoal + Tea Tree Scalp Treatment, which is included in the brand’s Scalp Revival product set and features detoxifying Binchotan charcoal that draws out impurities from the scalp. “This formulation contains a cooling blend of tea tree, peppermint and spearmint oils that help reduce itchiness, irritation and inflammation,” she says.

# The Best Ski Resorts in the US and Canada: 2025 Readers’ Choice Awards

Whether you’re a groomer snob, powder hound, or après connoisseur, these ski resorts from Maine to British Columbia tick all the boxes.

By [Jen Murphy](https://www.cntraveler.com/contributors/jen-murphy)

November 13, 2025

![Image 1: Santa Fe  New Mexico  USA](https://media.cntraveler.com/photos/6914ff0f6bd2d3ec1c0fa4e0/16:9/w_320%2Cc_limit/GettyImages-1185646736.jpg)

For our 39th annual [Reader’s Choice Awards](https://www.cntraveler.com/inspiration/readers-choice-awards), voters weighed in on their favorite ski resorts in North America—including the US and Canada. Colorado reigns as the top US ski destination, with 10 resorts making our top 30. And the East Coast held its ground, with two resorts breaking into the top 10 for the second straight year. The Southwest also made a strong showing with two entries this year. A handful of smaller, indie mountains made the list, too, proving bigger isn’t always better. From Whistler to Whitefish, and Taos to Telluride, these ski resorts were picked by our readers as the best in North America for their trails, lodges, lifts, and après-ski scenes. Whether you’re a powder snob or après aficionado, these ski resorts ticked all your boxes.

## 35. Copper Mountain, Colorado

Copper Mountain may be Colorado’s best-kept winter secret. Just 75 miles west of [Denver](https://www.cntraveler.com/gallery/best-things-to-do-in-denver), its off-the-highway location makes it easy to reach for both Colorado locals and visitors flying into Denver International Airport. With over 2,500 acres of terrain naturally divided by ability, Copper has long been a favorite for skiers and riders. Long a hub for elite ski and snowboarding training and competition, it’s often called the athlete’s mountain. This winter Copper will host three World Cup events leading into the 2026 Milano Cortina Olympics, including the inaugural Stifel Copper Cup presented ([November](https://www.cntraveler.com/gallery/best-places-to-travel-november) 27 through 30) with men’s and women’s alpine racing, followed by the Toyota U.S. Grand Prix ([December](https://www.cntraveler.com/gallery/best-places-to-travel-december) 17 through 20) featuring elite halfpipe competition. For those looking to progress their own skills, Woodward Copper offers a one-of-a-kind training center, complete with an indoor facility and terrain parks for every level.

**Where to stay:** The 127-room [Cambria Hotel Copper Mountain](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev) is just a short walk to Center Village and features on-site ski storage, an après bar, and hot tubs with mountain views.

**Stats:** 24 lifts for 153 trails. One-day lift ticket from $99; on the Ikon Pass.

## 34. Keystone Resort, Colorado

Thanks to its easy access just a quick and scenic drive from Denver, Keystone is one of Colorado’s most family-friendly resorts, with a Kids Ski Free program, slides and tunnels galore in the World’s Largest Mountaintop Snow Fort, and a ton of activities on and off the slopes that the whole family will love. The terrain, however, isn’t just for kids. With three mountains and five bowls, Keystone is easy to navigate and perfect for progression making it a winter playground for all-levels of skiers and riders. In 2024, Keystone elevated its on-mountain experience with the brand-new Bergman Express lift, making 550 acres of high alpine terrain accessible and approachable to a wide variety of skill levels from green trails to glades (rare for above tree line terrain). Now, transformations are underway in its River Run Village with the highly anticipated ski-in, ski-out Kindred Resort, slated to open this winter with new-to-Keystone amenities like a private club, valet parking, three restaurants, a luxury spa, valet ski check, and an upgraded home base for Keystone's Ski and Ride School. Keystone is also one of the state’s few resorts that offers night skiing. The action goes beyond schussing down the slopes. Families love the variety of activities offered: live music, snow tubing, horse-drawn sleigh rides, ice skating, and cross-country skiing at the Keystone Nordic Center.

**Where to stay:** Founded as an 1800s stagecoach stop, [Ski Tip Lodge](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev) remains one of the ski industry’s most historic buildings; the charming B&B is known for its excellent food and cozy fireside après scene. The opening of Kindred Resort—Keystone’s first major development in two decades—is all the hype this winter.

**Stats:** 21 lifts for 140 trails. One-day lift tickets from $96; on the Epic Pass.

## 33. Ski Santa Fe, New Mexico

A ski vacation in the southwest is underrated. And Taos isn’t the only high-desert hill to consider. Sitting at a base elevation of over 10,000 feet in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Ski Santa Fe flies under the radar. This family-owned and -operated resort is just 16 miles from downtown Santa Fe’s award-winning restaurants and rich art scene. Blessed with 300-plus days of sunshine a year and, typically, plenty of snowfall, it’s perfect for fairweather skiers looking for a dose of culture off the slopes. While most of the 660 acres are devoted to beginner and intermediate terrain, more advanced skiers and riders can pop into a handful of glades and a few double-black bowls.

**Where to stay:** For five-star resort pampering, book a stay at the [Four Seasons Resort Rancho Encantado](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev); [Bishop’s Lodge, an Auberge Resorts Collection](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev); or the [Inn of the Five Graces](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev).

**Stats:** Seven lifts for 83 trails. One-day lift ticket from $108.

## 32. Snowshoe Mountain, West Virginia

Snowshoe feels like a western ski resort but it’s nestled away on 11,000 acres in the [Appalachian Mountains](https://www.cntraveler.com/story/appalachian-mountains-may-have-once-been-as-tall-as-the-himalayas). The largest ski resort in the mid-Atlantic gets more snow and less ice than most other [East Coast resorts](https://www.cntraveler.com/gallery/best-new-england-resorts-from-maine-to-rhode-island). Skiers in the [greater DC area](https://www.cntraveler.com/gallery/best-things-to-do-in-washington-dc) happily make the four- to five-hour drive for the great terrain, excellent grooming, and charming village. With only black and double black terrain and 1,500 feet of vertical, the expert-only Western Territory offers some of the most challenging skiing in the region. There’s plenty of beginner-friendly terrain, too. This season, Snowshoe debuts a modern new ski lodge that will house the resort’s ski-and-ride school.

**Where to stay:** The ski-in/ski-out [Corduroy Inn & Lodge](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev) has three on-site restaurants, including a crowd-pleasing wood-fired pizza spot.

**Stats:** 14 lifts for 56 trails and four terrain parks. One-day lift ticket from $80.

## 31. Taos Ski Valley, New Mexico

Hard-core skiers who live for hike-to terrain and super steeps have always been fans of Taos Ski Valley. But recent resort investments, including a revitalized base area with an ice-skating rink, upgraded snowmaking and grooming, and improvements to beginner and intermediate terrain have made this New Mexico mountain destination way more family friendly. Taos Ski Valley leans into sustainability, equity, and inclusivity as the first ski resort in the world to have been B-Corp certified, and one of a few to be Certified CarbonNeutral®. The challenging terrain of Kachina Peak and the moguls of Al’s Run are the big draw for experts. For dining, the Bavarian is an institution known for its brats and German beers (they also host a sleigh ride dinner during the winter), and newcomer Corner Office gives the state its first natural wine bar. Down days are far from dull thanks to surrounding cultural attractions including the Taos Pueblo [UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://www.cntraveler.com/galleries/2014-12-23/most-beautiful-unesco-world-heritage-sites-galapagos-taj-mahal-yosemite).

**Where to stay:** Located adjacent to Lift 1, [The Blake](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev) offers a variety of accommodation options that include hotel rooms, suites, penthouses, and condos; decor blends rustic European architecture with one of North America’s finest collections of Southwestern art, including original works by Georgia O’Keeffe.

**Stats:** 13 lifts for 110 trails. One-day lift tickets from $115; on the Ikon Pass and Mountain Collective pass.

## 30. Heavenly Mountain Resort, California

Age is just a number, and Heavenly turns 70 years young this season. With nearly 5,000 acres of diverse terrain, Heavenly offers the best of both California and Nevada terrain including wide-open groomers, glades, and 1,600-foot mogul runs. Sparkling Lake Tahoe views, an average of 300 days of sunshine a year, and high-energy events and après make Heavenly a dream getaway for your party crew that is always looking for the next adventure. The unique Skyline Trail is a must-do run, taking in majestic mountain landscapes, flat valleys, and lake panoramas while crossing from California to Nevada. Plus, the Heavenly Village is located in the heart of South Lake Tahoe, surrounded by snow-based activities, restaurants, and fun events throughout the winter season. If the views of Lake Tahoe inspire you on the slopes, a trip to the shore is just minutes away.

**Where to stay:**[Basecamp South Lake Tahoe](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev) is just a four-minute walk to the gondola and offers a variety of rooms from bunks to luxe tents. [Zalanta Resort at the Village](https://cna.st/affiliate-?utm_source=nl&utm_term=CNT_Daily&utm_content=Final&utm_campaign=aud-dev) is steps away from Heavenly Village and residence-style rooms include gourmet kitchens and private balconies.

**Stats:** 28 lifts for 97 trails. One-day lift ticket from $127; on the Epic Pass.
